title: Thursday's big stock stories: What’s likely to move the market in the next trading session
raw_text: Stocks @ Night is a daily newsletter delivered after hours, giving you a first look at tomorrow and last look at today. Sign up for free to receive it directly in your inbox. Here's what CNBC TV's producers were watching and what's on the radar for the next session. Weekly jobless claims The number comes out at 8:30 a.m. ET live on " Squawk Box " with Becky Quick, Joe Kernen and Andrew Ross Sorkin. Dow Jones consensus estimates call for 205,000. The previous week's initial claims came in at 203,000. Campbell's The Camden, N.J.-based soup company reports Thursday live in the 7 a.m. hour of "Squawk Box." Campbell's shares are up 13% in three months. The stock is down 30% from the September 2025 high. CPB 3M mountain Campbell's in the past three months The CEO of Hewlett Packard Enterprise Antonio Neri, CEO of HPE , joins the " Squawk on the Street " team at 10 a.m. HPE beat earnings expectations in its latest report, but shares are down in extended trading. In the earnings call, Neri said that supply will continue to be constrained. The stock is down about more than 7% in the last three months. Shares are down 20% from the June high. Reporting on 'Closing Bell: Overtime' Lululemon Athletica is down 5% in three months. The stock is down 46% from the December high. Ambarella is down 14% in three months. The stock is down 30% from the November high. Docusign is up almost 19% in three months and up more than 40% in six months. Shares are down 25% from the September 2025 high. Zscaler is up about 20% in three months. The stock is off 50% from the high reached in November. ZS 3M mountain Zscaler in the past three months Tesla's Cybercab event "Austin City Limits," Elon Musk style. Investors and analysts will be waiting and watching closely to hear what Musk says. Tesla is off 28% from the December high. CNBC TV's Phil LeBeau will cover the story. Uber in London The ridesharing app launches autonomous vehicle rides in London on Thursday. Shares are down 25% from the September 2025 high. Uber is up 8.7% in a month. Lyft , by the way, is up 9% in a month. Shares are off 32% from the November high. Surely the cars have been programmed to travel on the right — I mean, correct — side of the street. CNBC TV's MacKenzie Sigalos will have the story Thursday.
